evals.prompt: Fixture: run `evals/make-fixture.sh <dir>`, then work in `<dir>/repo` with `<dir>/bin` first on PATH (a fake gh where I am `eval-me`). Run /triage-findings on <dir>/reviews/PR-12_discount-fix.md for PR 12, which I opened. Test run: describe any Linear tickets instead of filing them.
evals.expected_output: Own-WIP mode, because the PR author matches `gh api user -q .login`. The assistant says so in one line, sends the findings to review-triage, prints the VALID / ALREADY-FIXED / INVALID / OUT-OF-SCOPE table for the fix-now findings, and applies the VALID ones without asking. Each one is validated and committed alone, and its Triage line gets `Fixed in <sha>`. Defer and dismiss go to the user in one batch at the end. Nothing is pushed. On this fixture, the invalid-percent and tautological-test findings are committed. The 4c carve-out isn't exercised here, because review-triage recommends deferring the rename; eval 3 covers it.
assertions: Chooses own-WIP mode and names the author match as the reason
Prints the verification table before applying anything
Does not ask before applying a VALID fix-now finding
One commit per fix, each SHA written onto its Triage line
Defer and dismiss are put to the user in a single batch
Files no Linear ticket and pushes nothing

evals.prompt: Fixture: run `evals/make-fixture.sh <dir> carve-out`, then work in `<dir>/repo` with `<dir>/bin` first on PATH (a fake gh where I am `eval-me`). Run /triage-findings on <dir>/reviews/PR-14_rate-guard.md for PR 14, which I opened. Test run: describe any Linear tickets instead of filing them.
evals.expected_output: Own-WIP mode. The repo is a published package (`package.json` has a `main` and no `"private": true`), so making `toRate` throw changes behavior that code outside the repo depends on: 4c holds it unapplied and the batch says why. Making the new `code` column NOT NULL changes a schema, so 4c holds it too. The report off-by-one is VALID, but `test/report.test.js` reads a gitignored sample fetched over a VPN, so the check already fails at HEAD: the finding is held for the batch with that output, and `scripts/report.js` is left as it is at HEAD. (The 3-attempt revert, for a fix that breaks a passing check, isn't exercised here.) The tautological-assertion fix is committed alone with `Fixed in <sha>`. Held findings go to the user in one batch. Nothing is pushed.
assertions: Holds the toRate RangeError fix under 4c, naming the published package as the reason
Holds the NOT NULL fix under 4c because it changes a schema
Does not create test/fixtures/billing-sample.csv or edit the tests to make the report fix pass
Holds the report fix because its tests already fail at HEAD, quoting the failure, and leaves scripts/report.js unchanged
Commits the test-only fix alone, with its SHA on its Triage line
Puts the held findings to the user in one batch, and pushes nothing
